questions.question: Using the Nyquist formula, what is the maximum data rate of a noiseless 4 kHz channel using 4 signal levels?
Using the Nyquist formula, what is the maximum data rate of a noiseless 3 kHz channel using binary (2-level) signaling?
Using the Shannon capacity formula, what is the approximate maximum data rate of a 3 kHz channel with a 30 dB signal-to-noise ratio?
questions.explanation: 30 dB equals an SNR of 1000; C = 3000 x log2(1 + 1000) ~ 3000 x 9.97 ~ 30 kbps.

questions.question: What absolute signal-to-noise ratio does 30 dB correspond to in the Shannon formula?
questions.explanation: SNR(dB) = 10 log10(SNR), so 30 dB means SNR = 10^3 = 1000.

questions.question: Four 64 kbps voice channels are combined using synchronous TDM. What is the aggregate data rate?
questions.explanation: 4 channels x 64 kbps = 256 kbps of combined capacity.

questions.question: To reach 56 kbps on a noiseless 4 kHz channel per Nyquist, how many signal levels are required?
What is the total data rate of an ISDN Basic Rate Interface (2B+D)?
questions.explanation: BRI provides two 64 kbps B channels plus a 16 kbps D channel: 128 + 16 = 144 kbps.

questions.question: What is the approximate round-trip propagation delay for a GEO satellite link?
questions.explanation: Signals travel ~36,000 km up and down twice, yielding roughly 500+ ms round trip.

questions.question: A remote mining site needs Internet and chooses a Starlink-style constellation to minimize delay. Which orbit does it use?
questions.explanation: Starlink-class constellations use LEO satellites for low latency.

questions.question: A building's intercom lets occupants speak in both directions but only one at a time. What duplex mode is this?
questions.explanation: Half-duplex permits two-way traffic in alternating directions.

questions.question: An operator broadcasts simultaneously on one band where each handset decodes only calls bearing its assigned code. Which access method is in use?
questions.explanation: CDMA distinguishes simultaneous transmissions by spreading codes.

questions.question: An ISP carries dozens of separate channels as different colors of laser light down one fiber. What technique is this?
questions.explanation: WDM (or DWDM when dense) combines multiple wavelengths on one fiber.

questions.question: In what unit is signal attenuation typically measured?
questions.explanation: Attenuation is expressed as power loss in decibels per unit distance.

questions.question: Which formula determines the capacity of a noisy channel: Nyquist or Shannon?
questions.explanation: Shannon-Hartley (C = B log2(1 + S/N)) accounts for noise; Nyquist assumes noiseless.

questions.question: A VoIP call sounds choppy because packets arrive at uneven intervals even though bandwidth is sufficient. What is the culprit?
questions.explanation: Jitter is delay variation; buffers mitigate it but excessive jitter degrades audio.

questions.question: An amplifier provides a gain of 20 dB. By what factor is the signal's power increased?
questions.explanation: dB gain = 10 log10(Pout/Pin); 20 dB gives 10^(20/10) = 10^2 = 100 times the power.

questions.question: A signal suffers 3 dB of attenuation over a cable run. What fraction of its original power remains?
questions.explanation: A 3 dB loss equals a power ratio of 10^(-3/10) which is about 0.5 - approximately half the power survives.

questions.question: What is the total data rate of a North American T1 carrier line?
questions.explanation: A T1 carries 24 x 64 kbps channels plus 8 kbps framing, totaling 1.544 Mbps.

questions.question: A modem transmits at 2400 baud using 16-QAM, which encodes 4 bits per symbol. What is its bit rate?
questions.explanation: Bit rate = baud rate x bits per symbol = 2400 x 4 = 9600 bps.

questions.question: PCM digitizes voice by sampling at 8 kHz to produce a 64 kbps channel. How many bits does each sample carry?
questions.explanation: 64,000 bps / 8,000 samples per second = 8 bits per sample.
